title: Private deployments: VPC & on-prem deployment guide, day-2 ops, upgrade/rollback, and customer requirements library
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview
--------
This document aggregates Redwood Inference guidance for private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It covers reference architectures, on-prem packaging and hardening, a step-by-step VPC deployment guide, day-2 operations, upgrade and rollback procedures, and a customer requirements library to accelerate presales and SOW preparation. Target readers: platform engineers, solutions architects, and SREs supporting private deployments.

Goals
- Provide a repeatable, auditable deployment pattern for VPC and on-prem customers.
- Reduce operational risk via prescriptive day-2 runbooks and tested upgrade/rollback playbooks.
- Standardize customer requirements for networking, security, and capacity planning.

Owner & contacts
- Team: eng-private-deployments (Platform / Delivery)
- Oncall: private-deployments-oncall@redwood.internal
- Document owner: Asha Patel (Platform Architect)

Prerequisites
- Customer provides: VPC with at least two availability zones (AZs), NAT/egress, CIDR ranges, and peering or transit gateway as required.
- Access: Cross-account IAM role for provisioning (cloud) or root access to cluster nodes (on-prem) for initial install.
- Certificates: Customer-managed TLS certs (ACM or on-prem PKI) for control plane endpoints.

Reference architectures
- VPC deployment (recommended for cloud-hosted private control plane)
  - 3-tier design: edge (API gateways), control plane (management services), and compute (inference GPU pool).
  - AZ distribution for control plane services with an odd-numbered replica set for leader election (3 or 5).
  - Cross-AZ subnets: public subnets for load balancers, private subnets for control plane, isolated subnets for GPU nodes.
  - Networking: route tables per subnet, NAT gateways in each AZ, and security groups scoped to required ports only.
  - Data flows: customer traffic -> API GW (HTTPS 443) -> control plane services -> routing to dedicated GPU nodes over mTLS.

- On-prem deployment (air-gapped or customer-managed hardware)
  - Reference: single-rack minimum for PoC, multi-rack for production (N+1 GPU nodes across racks).
  - Network segmentation: management network, control plane network, inference network, monitoring/metrics network.
  - Storage: NFS/SMB for shared artifacts OR object store (S3 compatible) for model artifacts and logs.
  - Service placement: control plane can run on VMs or Kubernetes control plane nodes; inference runtime prefers GPU hosts with passthrough for NVLink (if available).

Packaging and distribution (on-prem)
- Deliverables
  - Installer: terraform + Ansible bundle (or Helm charts for customer Kubernetes).
  - Artifacts: signed container images, manifest lists for images per architecture, and checksums.
  - Documentation: install checklist, firewall rules, and post-install validation scripts.

- Hardening best practices
  - Minimum OS images: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS or RHEL 8.x (with kernel >= 5.15 for GPU driver compatibility).
  - Image signing and SBOM included in distribution.
  - Node security: disable unused services, enable auditd, and apply CIS benchmarks.
  - Secrets: integrate with KMS/HSM or customer vault; do not store plaintext secrets on disk.

VPC deployment guide (step-by-step)
1) Plan network and capacity (pre-call)
   - Confirm AZ count, CIDR ranges, and peering/transit gateway requirements.
   - Determine expected RPS and token throughput for capacity planning. See Capacity Sizing table below.
2) Prepare IAM and roles
   - Create cross-account role: redwood-private-deploy-role with admin/ec2/elb permissions.
   - Provide role ARN to delivery engineer.
3) Provision infrastructure
   - Apply terraform: terraform init && terraform apply -var-file=customer.tfvars.
   - Verify VPC, subnets, route tables, and NAT gateways are created.
4) Bootstrap control plane
   - Run installer: ./install-control-plane --env prod --cert /path/to/cert.pem --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-private-deploy-role
   - Wait for control plane readiness: curl -k https://control-plane-api.internal/healthz (expected: 200 and all checks pass).
5) Attach GPU compute pool
   - Register GPU nodes via bootstrap token: rdwctl node register --token <token> --labels gpu=true --pool inference-pool-1
   - Verify nodes accept workloads: rdwctl cluster nodes | grep inference-pool-1
6) Configure routing, caching, and quotas
   - Set route policies in console: latency-first for critical routes.
   - Configure KV caching TTLs and prefix caching for high-RPS apps.
7) Post-install verification
   - Run smoke tests: rdwctl test generate --model redwood-v1-small --prompt "Hello" --expected-prefix "Hello"
   - Validate metrics ingestion into customer Prometheus/CloudWatch.

Day-2 operations (SRE checklist)
- Monitoring & alerting
  - Required metrics: request_latency_p50/p95/p99, token_consumption_rate, node_gpu_utilization, kv_cache_hit_rate, control_plane_healthy_replicas.
  - Default SLOs: 99.9% availability for control plane, 95th percentile inference latency <= 200ms for short context (<=512 tokens) on dedicated capacity.
  - Alert thresholds (examples):
    - control_plane_healthy_replicas < 2 -> P1
    - node_gpu_utilization > 90% for 10m -> P2 (scale)
    - kv_cache_hit_rate < 30% -> P3 (investigate eviction policy)
- Backups and disaster recovery
  - Control plane DB backups: nightly snapshots retained 14 days.
  - Model artifacts: replicate to secondary object store or S3 bucket with versioning enabled.
  - Test recovery quarterly with playbook 'control-plane-restore'.
- Scaling and autoscaling
  - GPU pool autoscaling policy: target_cpu_utilization 60%, scale_up_cooldown 5m, max_nodes configured per contract.
  - Burst policy: allow use of shared spare capacity for short bursts (<30s) if enabled in contract.
- Routine maintenance
  - Weekly: verify cert expiry dates and rotate if within 30 days.
  - Monthly: security patching window coordinated with customer; expect 30-60m node drain times.

Upgrade and rollback procedures
- Principles
  - Always run upgrades in canary first (1-2 nodes or 5-10% of traffic).
  - Maintain immutable artifacts with semantic versions and checksums.
  - Keep DB migrations backward compatible where possible and include feature flags for activation.

- Pre-upgrade checklist
  1. Verify backups: DB snapshot completed and model artifacts replicated.
  2. Confirm health: control_plane_healthy_replicas == desired and no P1/P2 alerts active.
  3. Notify stakeholders: success metrics and rollback thresholds defined.

- Upgrade (canary) procedure
  1. Deploy control plane update to canary nodes: rdwctl upgrade control-plane --version vX.Y.Z --canary 2
  2. Run smoke tests and synthetic workloads for 30m.
  3. Monitor error rates and latency: if error_rate increase > 0.5% absolute or latency p95 increases > 20%, abort.
  4. Promote to remaining replicas in staged batches (AZ by AZ).

- Rollback procedure
  1. Trigger rollback: rdwctl rollback control-plane --to-version vA.B.C.
  2. If rollback fails, isolate traffic to fallback region or degrade to a compatible model variant.
  3. Post-rollback: run integrity checks and reconcile DB schema if necessary.

Customer requirements library (summary table)
- Use this table during pre-sales to collect minimal requirements.

| Requirement area | Minimal requirement | Notes | Owner |
|------------------|---------------------|-------|-------|
| Network | 2 AZs, private subnets, NAT | Provide CIDR & peering details | Customer network team |
| IAM & Access | Cross-account role or service account | ARN or service account email required | Customer cloud admin |
| Certificates | TLS cert (ACM or PEM) | Provide cert + chain + key (or integration details) | Security / PKI |
| Capacity | GPU type and count; baseline RPS | See Capacity Sizing table | Customer infra |
| Storage | S3 or S3-compatible object store | Versioning recommended | Customer infra |
| Monitoring | Prometheus endpoint or CloudWatch permissions | Metrics and alerting integration | Customer SRE |
| Compliance | SOC2 / ISO checklists | Provide certs & control evidence | Security team |
| Backup | Snapshot schedule & retention | Nightly, 14 days min | Customer/backups team |

Capacity Sizing (example)
- Inputs to collect: avg tokens per request, avg requests per second, expected concurrency, model family (memory/compute).
- Example baseline table:

| Workload profile | Expected RPS | Avg tokens | Suggested GPU type | Nodes (baseline) |
|------------------|----------:|----------:|--------------------|----------------:|
| Interactive chat (low latency) | 50 | 64 | A10G / A100-40GB | 2-4 |
| High throughput batch | 500 | 32 | A100-80GB | 4-8 |
| Embeddings heavy | 200 | N/A | V100 / A10G | 2-6 |

Validation checklist (post deployment)
- All control plane services return healthy (healthz endpoints).
- GPU nodes are registered and labelled correctly.
- Prometheus metrics available and dashboards ingesting data.
- E2E synthetic tests pass (latency and correctness).

Playbooks & runbooks (links)
- control-plane-restore (quarterly DR test)
- node-drain-and-replace (node lifecycle)
- canary-upgrade-and-promote (upgrade playbook)
- incident-escalation-private-deploy (incident procedures)

Appendix A: Example CLI snippets
- Register node:
  rdwctl node register --token abc123 --labels gpu=true --pool inference-pool-1
- Quick health check:
  curl -sSf https://control-plane-api.internal/healthz | jq .status
- Upgrade canary:
  rdwctl upgrade control-plane --version v1.4.2 --canary 2

Appendix B: Example Kubernetes manifest (inlined Helm values)
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: rdw-controlplane-config
data:
  log_level: "info"
  cache_ttl_seconds: "3600"

Appendix C: Escalation matrix
- P1: immediate paging to oncall + eng-private-deployments lead.
- P2: Slack notify private-deployments channel and next business hour response.

Notes
- This document is intended to be vendor/bundle agnostic where possible; specific customer engagements will require tailoring. If customer requires air-gapped installation, follow the 'on-prem packaging' checklist strictly and coordinate with Security for offline signing keys.
